title: Who Audits the Auditor? Automated Assurance and the Displacement of Accountability in Enterprise AI
content: Organisations are beginning to automate assurance itself - to build artificial intelligence (AI) systems that audit documents, check compliance and score conformance, the very controls once performed by people held answerable for their judgement. The presented study is a critical account of what this move does to accountability. Reading the practice through Power's theory of the audit society and against the author's own experience designing a multi-agent document-compliance checker for a regulated bank, the study argues that automating assurance carries a specific hazard - the production of accountability theatre, in which the appearance of control substitutes for its substance because the automated auditor is trusted precisely where a human auditor would be questioned. The paper develops the mechanism of this displacement, shows why transparency alone does not cure it, and argues that an automated assurance system must be held to the same standard of governed autonomy it enforces on the documents it inspects, on pain of becoming an unexamined authority inside the organisation. Drawing on work on responsible AI, the account closes with principles for what beneficent automated assurance would require. The argument is normative and it is meant to be resisted.
